At the lunch break, I had those colour prints made, and would ask that they be substituted into everyone's respective binder.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr Prosecutor. So you are going to carry on with the examination-in-chief. How much more time, approximately, do you need?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Approximately half an hour, judge, maybe between half an hour and 45 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Rather half an hour than 45 minutes?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I was thinking maybe 45 minutes rather than half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Try and really focus on the questions that are in support of the Prosecution, that is what I keep repeating. Let us say last offer 30 minutes. Sergeant Major, please sit down.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Sergeant Major.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: This afternoon you and I together are going to attempt to slow down for the sake of the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: One last question on the trip you had into Putis and Loncari. After the time that you went in there around the 16th April and saw the houses burnt and looted, did you have occasion to go into that house thereafter -- excuse me, that village, thereafter, days down the line?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, a number of days down the line we were tasked to go into that district or that area again. At this stage it was to see if the opposing forces had retreated back to their original lines of defence.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: All of the property that you saw looted, was it gone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us turn ahead to your testimony concerning 18th April 1993, the date of the truck bomb. You were tasked to go into Vitez that day.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: For what reason?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The reason of the tasking was that it was believed that in the area of the flats in Vitez there was a young Muslim boy belonging to one of the commanders, and the commander was concerned, due to the current situation, for that boy's safety.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: You also told us that there were checkpoints at two locations that you tried to get through to get into Vitez.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr President, if we can turn our attention to the third map, with the assistance of the usher, which is Exhibit 56F. Thank you. Mr President, if I could ask Sergeant Major Hughes to go up to the chart, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Sergeant Major Hughes, you said that there was a checkpoint that prevented you getting into Stari Vitez that was manned by the Croats, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: Can you, using the red pen, show the court approximately where this Croat checkpoint was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Witness marks map).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Get a little closer, Mr Hayman, if you wish to.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Could you mark that with the number 1?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Witness marks map).

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: What type of vehicle was blocking the road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was a large petrol tanker.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: You then said that you attempted to get into Vitez through another way, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. I came back on myself, went round the bypass and tried to come in via the east.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: What happened then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As we approached off the main bypass into Vitez, where there is a bridge, there was a tractor blocking the bridge and on the ground were a number of anti-tank mines.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: Were there any soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were one or two soldiers in the area the other side of the checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: Using 56F, could you mark that checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is obviously slightly off the map.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: Would it be off the top left side of the map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here (indicates) where the river comes through, the road will come along a bit further.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: There is another checkpoint up there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, with the tractor and the landmines.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: After that checkpoint, did you go back to the other checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, what we then did is moved back, moved back to the area of the garage, the echelon, and at that stage, we were then told to move forward and try again, and this time try and negotiate through the checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, we could not. They would not let us through the checkpoint at that stage.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: What happened then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What we discovered is in the meantime, while we were round to the eastern part of Vitez, they had decided to move the tanker from its original position here to forward of the junction (witness marks map).

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: Can you mark that as number 2? Did that change what you and the other Warriors that were in your platoon could do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Looking at the map, it then gave us the opportunity to move back to this area here (indicates), and then move round the field on to the road down to the junction and in, thereby outflanking the checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: Could you use the yellow marker and mark hard, if you could, the area that you went around and back up into Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Witness marks map).

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: Why do you not try that in green so we can see it? Could you put an arrow at the top on the direction that you took? Sergeant, when you got past this checkpoint, what did those soldiers that were in the checkpoint do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Once we were beyond the checkpoint, they engaged us with small arms fire, to the rear of the vehicle. I observed through my rear periscopes, after they engaged they then dispersed into the buildings either side of the road. I just sent a report over the radio and continued with the task in hand.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: Sergeant Major, when you say that they engaged you, they shot at you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: Based on that, did you conclude that they were not happy with your Warriors bypassing that checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, definitely.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you then proceed into Vitez and look for this young boy?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. We moved into the area of the flats to the east of Vitez, where a liaison officer dismounted from the vehicle, went to the entrance of the flats and from that point, I had a discussion with a number of HVO soldiers, and from what information I got is that it was unsuccessful of gaining entry into the flats, and then we returned back to the school.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you return back on the same road that you took in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: What about the checkpoint at the area that you have marked 1 and 2?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was completely clear.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: The petrol tanker was gone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was gone.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: Where did you go with your Warriors?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We went back initially to the school to drop off the LO officer and then I moved back to go the echelon garage, to (i) refuel and (ii) to assess the damage caused to the rear of the vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: The echelon garage is marked there on the chart, is it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: Sergeant Major, if you could take a seat again. Sergeant Major, you testified that shortly thereafter you heard this explosion, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you go into Stari Vitez at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not exactly at that time, but I was then tasked to go in and investigate the cause of the explosion.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: So it would be fair to say that you went in shortly thereafter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: Not that day but the next day, did you take a series of photographs of the damage that you observed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr President, if we could turn at this point to photographs 152/4, 5, 6 and 7.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Who took those photographs, Mr Kehoe?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: These photographs were taken by the witness, Mr President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. Carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Is that correct, Sergeant Major?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: Once again Sergeant Major, after my question could you just pause a moment, we could move along. If we can go to the first photograph, which is 152/4. That is just the first one on top. Can we focus in a little bit on that? Sergeant Major, is that a photograph you took the day after the explosion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: Is there a dead body depicted in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there is a dead body in that photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: Could you use the pointer and point to the location in the photograph where you observed a dead body?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Indicates).

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. If we can go to the next photograph, 152/5, Sergeant Major, does that photograph you took depict the damage you observed, in part, when you entered Stari Vitez on 18th April?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: Can we go to the next photograph, 152/6? Sergeant Major, that photograph that you took the day after the explosion, does that likewise depict another aspect of the damage in Stari Vitez that you observed on 18th April 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: And the last photograph, yet another photograph that you took, does that ascertain the location of the general area that this truck bomb took vis-a-vis the rest of Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, sir -- that is okay for now, Mr Usher. Did you assist, with other members of the British battalion, in the removal of refugees from Stari Vitez on 18th April 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: During 18th April 1993, did you see other Bosnian Muslims hiding in the basements of Stari Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, a number in basements, and on the outer limits of the blast area were people in gardens et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: Did many of those people refuse to leave?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would say a small amount refused to leave. These were mainly the older people that decided that they, despite the damage, wanted to remain in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: I think you testified, Sergeant Major, that on the next day, the 19th, you went and picked up dead bodies and pieces of bodies in Stari Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: Moving ahead, Sergeant Major, you know that there had been a cease-fire conference at the British battalion on 21st April 1993.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: After that time, Sergeant Major, did you and the other platoon leaders go out and patrol the area to see where actual troops were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we went out on numerous tasks in the surrounding area to see how the cease-fire was taking effect.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: Was part of the tasking for the British battalion to assist in allowing both the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the HVO to retreat from the confrontation lines?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: As part of that, were General Halilovic, on behalf of the Bosnians, and General Petkovic taken out to their locations to convince their soldiers to withdraw, or talk to their soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. I was tasked to pick up both commanders, using two Warriors, so the HVO were in one vehicle and the BiH commanders were in the other vehicle. We also had an interpreter and a member of the ECMM.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: You said that the HVO commander was General Petkovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: Where did you pick General Petkovic up to take him on this job of seeing these various HVO locations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We picked him up from the hotel in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you go into the Hotel Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Initially on picking him up, no. However, later in the day, when we came to the end of the task, to visit the hotel, we had cause then to go inside, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: When you went inside, Sergeant Major, did you see any HVO soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were a number of HVO soldiers in the entrance to the hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: How were these soldiers dressed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Two in particular I noticed were dressed in black.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you see any soldiers in the Hotel Vitez in camouflage?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were a number of soldiers in camouflage, maybe one or two.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: So it would be fair to say that there were both camouflage dressed and black clad soldiers in the Hotel Vitez when you dropped General Petkovic off.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we could, with the court's permission, if we could place Exhibit 80/5 on the ELMO, and I do believe it has been picked out, this is an exhibit that is already in evidence. Sergeant Major, do you recognise General Petkovic in Exhibit 80/5?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: Can you use the pointer and point to the man who is General Petkovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Indicates).

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: Is that the man, Sergeant Major, that you picked up at the Hotel Vitez, that you took into the bungalow and ultimately brought back to the Hotel Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: Sergeant Major, I know you had a number of difficult tasks, but you referred this morning to a task that you had relating to a body exchange that took place approximately 28th April. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I recall.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: I think you stated that you picked up three Croat bodies and you took them to the school in Vitez, where you picked up somewhere between 94 and 96 bodies, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: When you picked up those 94 to 96 bodies, did you have the opportunity to look at the condition of any of those bodies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I had the opportunity, due to the fact that all the bodies were wrapped in clear plastic.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: What was the condition of those bodies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The condition was that a number of the bodies -- a majority of the bodies were recent in the fact that I would say a number of days, three, four days, obviously in that condition. Judging by the type of clothing, the majority were civilian, women, older men and young, maybe teenage, bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: Were some of those bodies decapitated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, on the first drop off of bodies in the area where they were going to bury the bodies that we collected, the initial couple of bodies taken off the vehicle, I first thought that they were small children. However, on close examination the two small packages were actually the heads of two bodies, next to, obviously, the small packages.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: In fact did some of those bodies appear to be children or younger people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would say that some appeared to be younger people rather than children.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr President, with the court's permission, before we go to the next exhibit, Sergeant Major, your job was to bring those bodies to a particular location in Stari Vitez, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: Did the British battalion assist in the burial of those 94 to 96 bodies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In a sense, yes, by using the engineer field tractor to excavate two large graves.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: Did the British battalion serve as a protective ring around the cemetery while the engineers were digging this grave and the bodies were being buried?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the point of the arrival of the bodies, the only two vehicles were my own vehicles, and we just positioned them as there was a feeling that, or a worry by the Muslims that they could be shot at from the northern area of the -- sorry, the southern area of the town itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr President, at this time if we could move to a video clip, which is Exhibit 153. This is a video clip of that burial that was received from the government of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr Hayman?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I do not know what that is a reference to, "received from the government".

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That is the source, Mr President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: That is the source. Do you want a more specific source, Mr Hayman?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I am not enquiring as to the source at all, I just did not understand if Mr Kehoe was attempting to authenticate the tape or if the witness was going to authenticate the tape.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Let us view that clip and then we will turn to the witness. At any rate, the judges want to see that clip. So Mr Kehoe, can you turn to the technicians and ask them to let us view this and then you will put a question of the witness, as we did with the photographs. Thank you, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr President, I believe the technicians are prepared to put it on. At any time you gentlemen are ready.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Sergeant Major, does that film clip appear to be an accurate depiction of the burial of those 94 to 96 bodies that you brought on or about 28th April 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: In fact, Sergeant Major, we saw two loads of bodies there, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: Can you explain to the judges --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: May the witness put his microphone on, please? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Can you explain to the judges, Sergeant Major, the bringing in of both loads of the bodies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. We arrived at the school in Vitez, and took up positions either side of the entrance to the school. The lorry with the trailer which was seen in the film was there. On arrival, there was another vehicle at the entrance to the school. This was an old refrigerated-type vehicle that had been preloaded with some of the bodies. At that stage, it was decided to take some of the bodies from that vehicle and place them on to the vehicle that had been driven to the school by the Muslims. They then started to load the large vehicle and trailer. Once this was completed, we then escorted those vehicles to the field as depicted in the video.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: Sergeant Major, there were bodies or body parts in all of the plastic bags that we just saw on this video?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I can turn, Mr President, to our two last photographs that are in the binders, and that would be 152/8 and 152/9. Sergeant Major, does 152/8 depict a graveyard in Stari Vitez after the holes were filled in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: Another angle of that is 152/9, if I could put that on the ELMO, Mr Usher. Likewise, Sergeant Major, is that a photograph of the two rows of graves that the engineers dug that day for the bodies that you brought to the graveyard in Stari Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr President, if I might just consult with my colleagues for one moment. (Pause). Mr President, your Honours, I would like to introduce into evidence the maps, copies of the maps that have been sketched upon by Sergeant Major Hughes and for the record, they are 45F, 53C, 56F and 59B, and I would likewise offer into evidence Exhibit 152. With that, Mr President, I have no further questions of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Did I understand it well, Registrar, the video clip is part of the exhibits?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I apologise, Mr President, I will offer that as well, as Exhibit 153.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well, the exhibits are now in evidence. If I understood you well, you have finished, no further questions to the witness. We can now move on to the cross-examination and I believe that it is Mr Hayman who is going to take the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: It is, thank you, your Honour. Good afternoon, Sergeant Major. The bodies you have just described and we have all seen, were you told what geographic area the 94 to 96 Muslim bodies had been gathered from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was not told that information.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Were you told from what geographic area the three Croat bodies had come from, or been gathered from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One Croat body was taken from a shallow grave inside the Muslim quarter, but not where he had been killed, that destination I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Were all three of the Croat bodies picked up in the same place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they were picked up in separate places.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: One was taken from a shallow grave within Stari Vitez, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: And the other two?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The other two were picked up in the area of Stari Vitez, but away from the first body.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Thank you. You mentioned a moment ago seeing soldiers at the Hotel Vitez on 28th April, I think, 1993.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did you go in past the front door at the hotel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, on the second occasion to visit the hotel, we were taken inside, through the reception area of the hotel, and taken into what was, I presume, would have been the restaurant, and we remained there for 45 minutes to an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Was the restaurant part of the HVO command, or was it functioning as a restaurant?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was not functioning as a restaurant. We were the only individuals in there, and at one stage a HVO soldier came in with some food and a litre bottle of coca-cola.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did it appear to be a closed restaurant to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Definitely a closed restaurant.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: So it sounds like you did not gain entry into a functioning portion of the HVO command within the hotel, is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I object to counsel's question, because the witness said he did enter into the HVO headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: He went in the hotel and sat in an empty restaurant, your Honour. I think the question should be answered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, the question should be answered, but we should not dwell too long on this question. Please, Sergeant Major, answer briefly and let us move on to the next question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could I have the question again, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Other than to go in the front door and sit in an empty restaurant, did you enter any other portions of the hotel that were being used as a military command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, apart from going through the main entrance and on to the restaurant, I was aware that on entering the front door of the Hotel Vitez that I was in HVO headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you have some special training or a period of preparation before the Cheshires departed for Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we had training prior to our deployment.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: How many weeks did you train for the deployment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Approximately two months.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Let me direct your attention to 16th April 1993. When you entered Vitez for the first time as you have described, who else was with you? What other Warrior vehicles?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was my own call sign, followed by a second call sign from my platoon, which was Romeo Two One. Also there were two vehicles from call sign Romeo One Zero.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: So a total of four vehicles?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I recollect, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Can you tell us who commanded the other vehicles, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Romeo One Zero was commanded by Lieutenant Dooley. The other vehicle commanders I cannot recall.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did you go by the Hotel Vitez on mid morning on 16th April 1993 when you went into Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I went up to the end of the road to the junction where the Hotel Vitez was, moved around and then came back on myself on the southern road.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: From the vantage point you had, could you see that there were HVO soldiers in the area outside the Hotel Vitez who appeared to be taking cover on the morning of 16th April 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not that I noticed. I was more concerned with another area than the area of the hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Later in the day on the 16th, two HVO soldiers were shot, travelling from a Warrior back into the Hotel Vitez. Was your platoon involved in the transportation of those two HVO negotiators back from the BritBat school to the Hotel Vitez, if you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was not involved in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, if the usher could assist by returning Exhibit 45F, which is already on the easel, to the top photograph, that would be helpful. Let me direct your attention to, on that photograph, the area you I believe coloured in a pink square -- thank you -- or bell shaped drawing. Do you recall that and see it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: This is the area in which you described seeing a number of HVO soldiers moving in an organised fashion, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: How many soldiers did you see? Were there six, approximately?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Approximately six, maybe more.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Give us your best estimate. Is six your best estimate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I will go with six, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: On your visit to Vitez on the morning of 16th April, did you see any other soldiers other than those six at any time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not after I moved off from that location.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did these six, in the manner in which they were moving, were they appearing to protect themselves and use structures or obstructions to protect themselves from possible fire?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, in the manner that they were moving, to me as a professional soldier trained for various aspects of warfare, one being fighting in built-up areas, their movement was that of a unit, no matter how small, that was tactically moving or advancing on to a position that they wished to take.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Were they simply walking in the open?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they were moving tactically in a manner as what we would call, "fire and manoeuvre".

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Were they staying close to the walls of the buildings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were moving from cover to cover.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: So they were taking cover as they moved along, would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Rather than cover from fire they were just taking up the normal position to cover their fellow soldiers as they advanced in the direction that they were going.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: But as they did that, they did not do that out in the open, they took some position where they themselves had some protection?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I object, your Honour. I object to the repetition. If counsel does not like the answer -- the witness's answer is the witness's answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, the witness has answered the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I will go on, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: These tactics are used, "fire and manoeuvre" apparently is the answer, so the objection is sustained.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I will move on, your Honour, but "cover" is a term of art. I would like to state the grounds of my -- it is an offer of proof, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The judge has ruled.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: May I state my offer of proof, your Honour, and then I will move on? I just want to make the record clear. "Cover" can mean covering an individual from fire or one soldier providing cover for another. It was a term of art and I was trying to clarify it, that is my offer of proof. I will move on. Did you see these six soldiers on the morning of 16th April 1993, did you see them fighting? Did you see them fire their weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they did not fire their weapons, they just moved in a manner of fire and manoeuvre. In them situations, whether you are engaging an enemy or not engaging an enemy, or you are being engaged, you would still move in that fashion.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did they fire off any grenades?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see any grenades being fired off.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did you see any of the buildings that they were in start to burn?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did you conclude that the type of activity they were in was a normal action, or would be a normal action in a built-up area, for one military to check and see if an opposing military force was present?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would put my professional ability on it that they, at that time, due to the situation on first arriving in Vitez, that they were moving with the idea of taking ground.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Can you answer my question any more directly? Do you recall what the question was?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr Hayman, can you move on to another question? I am sorry, this has happened several times, you have explained what you are aiming at and I think we believe we understand what your objectives are, but there was an answer provided by the witness. I am so sorry, you have to move on to another question.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I will move on, your Honour, but with all due respect, the answer was not responsive to my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The question might not have been very well put, so you have to move to another one.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: You said these soldiers had ribbons on their shoulders, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Had you seen these types of ribbons on the shoulders of soldiers in the Lasva Valley before, before 16th April 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On occasion, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Had you seen them routinely at checkpoints?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not at checkpoints, no.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: For how long did you observe these six soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I observed them maybe just a couple of minutes. I was continually on the move, moving round that area of the town of Vitez to get a full assessment of the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: These two minutes, were you stationary or were you catching glimpses of them while you were on the move or what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was on the move, I was never stationary until later on in the tasking. As I said, I was moving round to get a bigger picture of the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: You have drawn a fairly good-sized area within the pink bell-shaped drawing on Exhibit 45F. Did you see these six men in all parts of that bell-shaped drawing during those two minutes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not in the whole area of the bell shape.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Why is the area so large? Is it because you are not sure what areas they were within during that two minute period?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The area is so large because at that time I was covering again a large area on observation. The reason I have marked that area is because that was the area, basically, of my responsibility and the area that I moved round and checked. On checking that area, it was in and around more to the east of that bell shape.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did they travel during that two minutes the whole length of the bell, if you will, from the top to the bottom, along the eastern portion of the bell, or can you give us any more specificity in that regard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They may have travelled that far. I obviously moved --

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did you see them travel that far?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see them travel that far.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: What portion of the bell, down the eastern side of the bell, did you see them travel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Do you want me to indicate?

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Or if you can tell us half, a third, a quarter, that is fine.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A quarter.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: We looked at a photograph with you of what appeared to be a dead child, a boy, it was Exhibit 152, photos 1 and 2. You said that it was on the edges of Vitez, something like that. Can you describe where that was? Did you see it on your drive in or out of Vitez, or somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The body was actually on the southern side of Vitez, where the road comes down from the area of the hotel, past the sports pitch or the sports stadium, continue on down and where the road peters out into the open area, going west towards the quarry, the body, as I was going out that direction, was on the left-hand side of the road.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: So well below the sports stadium in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Exhibit 45F, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did you determine the ethnicity of that victim?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did you learn anything of the circumstances of his death?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: You also described a wounded woman crawling on the concrete and described her as being in the lower left-hand corner of the pink bell on Exhibit 45F, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Could you tell where -- first of all, what type of fire was going on in the area when you saw her; was it rifle fire or some other kind of fire?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was rifle fire or small arms fire, as we call it.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Could you tell where it was coming from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, the problem being that when you close down, you have got a headset on, vehicle noise, although we tended to keep the hatch open slightly to try and get an idea of outside noise. But it was difficult to ascertain the direction.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: On the morning of the 16th, did you visit the BiH Army headquarters in Stari Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: On the 16th, did you see any Croat refugees from Vrhovine entering Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Let me direct your attention forward a day to 17th April 1993. If the usher could assist by turning the current map on the easel so that Exhibit 53C is depicted. You have circled on this exhibit the location where you saw an anti-aircraft gun. I believe this is the right exhibit. At the very uppermost portion of this photograph, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Can you describe where in relation to the gun you saw the individual you believed was a spotter for the gun?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Do you wish me to get up?

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: If it is helpful to show us on the photograph, that is fine. If it is a few inches in one direction or another from the circle, you can describe it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Witness marks map).

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: I am sorry, your hand was obstructing my view when you drew it. You drew a small circle within the circle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Within that area.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: I thought you said a spotter would be deployed some distance from the gun towards the firing site, so that the spotter would have a superior view of the area in which the fire was directed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: So what does this tell you, what do you conclude from where this person you concluded was a spotter was located with respect to this gun on this day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The spotter or forward observer is observing for weapons which are on what we would call a gun line, i.e. those on the hill were spotting, as I mentioned, the two possible mortar rounds that were fired. They were not spotting for the anti-aircraft gun.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Sorry, I could not get the translation. There is nothing coming on channel 5. That is it, it is back again.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Where did we lose you, your Honour? Shall I repeat my question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. Carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: So the spotter you described was not spotting for the anti-aircraft gun, in your opinion, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, in my opinion the spotter was spotting or observing for what I would class as either an artillery weapon or a mortar.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did you observe -- you observed the anti-aircraft gun you described. Did you also observe a location from which either artillery or mortars were being fired at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, due to the fact that if the spotters were in the position they were in, then the either artillery or mortar pieces tactically would not be able to be seen from where the observers were.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did you see any rounds land from where you were, down by the bungalow, on this occasion, either from an anti-aircraft gun, a mortar or an artillery?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Do you know where the location of Barangi is above Ahmici, up the hill and away from the road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not recall the name.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: How far above and beyond Ahmici could, in your opinion, this anti-aircraft gun, at the location you have indicated on Exhibit 53C, could it have reached across the valley?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On a weapon of that type, it could have a maximum range of 2,000 metres to be effective, but it could go beyond that range. But any range beyond the 2,000, then it would become more difficult to make sure that the rounds you were firing would be accurate and hit the target you were aiming at.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Also on 17th April 1993, you went to Sivrino Selo; do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: You saw some civilians in a house.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did you go in and talk to them, with the assistance of an interpreter, to find out what their situation was exactly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, the majority of taskings we did not have interpreters. We tended to, if necessary, relay messages back to the headquarters and we would then move on with normal tasking.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did you investigate whether there was a BiH Army presence in Sivrino Selo on that occasion, or did you not investigate that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not investigate that.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Now let me turn your attention to your visits in or near Putis and Jelinak, which you have described. Do you have any way of putting a more precise date, or any precise date, on the first occasion when you went by Putis and Jelinak and you saw a red glow or a reflection of something burning in the sky?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot put an accurate date, but I would say it would be either two or a day before the 16th.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: So it was before the 16th that you saw this fire, the reflections of a fire?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: On your second visit to the area, can you tell us, did you go into Jelinak, Putis, Loncari or all of them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I went into Putis and Jelinak.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: You said there were burned houses in both, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Were all the houses burned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not all houses were burned.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Was it a small fraction that were burned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I would say a small fraction of the houses.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Are you able to put a number on it, 5 or 3 or 10 per cent, or are you not able?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not able.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Were there any civilians left living in either village, Putis or Jelinak?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Do you know whether those villages were mixed ethnically, or were inhabited solely by one ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mixed.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Both were mixed, as far as you knew?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Jelinak was mixed.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: When you went back a second time, you would date that as how many days after your first drive by, if I may call it a drive by?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would say any time after the 19th.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: But it was after the 19th April that you actually went into the villages, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Do you know which army controlled those villages as of that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, there was no one in the village at all.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: You referenced the burnt out condition of the houses, those that had been burned. I take it that what you meant was houses of a similar construction when burned look the same, is that what you meant?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not understand your question, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: The houses in this region generally tend to be cinder block or cement construction with either a wooden or a wooden reinforced -- wooden infrastructure roof, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: When those houses burn, if they do burn, the floors in the roof typically collapsed into the shell which remains?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Is that the type of burned house that you saw of those that had been burned in these two villages?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From what I can recall, maybe one or two of them were, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Were the others some other kind of houses that had burned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that particular stage, in that situation, to me, a burnt house was a burnt house.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: You did not mean to imply any other distinguishing characteristic between burned houses in Ahmici and burned houses in Jelinak or Putis, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Thank you. You visited Stari Vitez both on the day of the truck bomb explosion and the following day, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: On either day, to your knowledge, was any type of forensic investigation or other inquiry concerning the bomb itself undertaken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: There were other things that you and others were occupied with, is that why you chuckled?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was a very busy time, very traumatic time, and in those sorts of situations unfortunately you do not have the forensic experience available to you.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Thank you. On 28th April -- I have just a few more questions -- 1993, you said you visited certain frontline positions with Generals Petkovic and Halilovic. As you sit here, are you able to recall any of those specific positions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Can you tell us those that you can recall, or if you would like to show them to us on a map, please do so, we can hopefully find a map among these that would be suitable. Is this map suitable, which is Exhibit 53C?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is suitable.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Please proceed, if you can point out any locations which are frontline positions visited by you together with Generals Petkovic and Halilovic on 28th April 1993.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One of the frontlines was this position here on the high ground by the pylon (indicates).

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Before you go on, Sergeant Major, if we can just try and assign a location, I do not want to draw on the Prosecutor's exhibit, and I do not think we need take the time to put an overlay on it. Can you help orient us as to where this location is? First of all, can the judges see? We need to make sure of that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The road junction of the Dubravica road, which goes across the mountains to Zenica, there again from the same junction, the road on the Dubravica junction, which is the Vitez bypass which goes around the mountain to Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: So you are indicating the high ground to the east of the Vitez mountain road above the villages of Santici and to the west of Santici, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Okay, that is one location. Can you point out any others? Do you know as you look, is this the area of Vrhovine and Poculica on the Zenica mountain road, or those are not familiar to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Names, unless they are ...

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Very well. Can you point out another location which you recall visiting on that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We went along this area (indicates).

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Indicating on this map the edges of a dark shaded area and a light, lighter shaded area to the north of Ahmici and Pirici, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Any other locations that you recall visiting on that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We visited Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: When you say Vitez, do you mean Stari Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Stari Vitez, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Was there a walking tour of the frontline in Stari Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was a walking tour of the area of Stari Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Can you tell us what that involved? Perhaps you can turn to the court and I will return to the lectern?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That involved initially going to the BiH headquarters, where both sets of commanders entered the headquarters. After a short period of time, they came out of the building and then we progressed from the BiH headquarters and moved around various parts of Vitez and again at another point, another building was entered, and again for a short period of time a discussion took place, and then from there we returned to the vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Was there any inspection while you were in the area of the BiH headquarters in Stari Vitez of any defensive lines, trenches or other fortifications that may have been erected by that point in time, or was that not done?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was not done.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Thank you. In addition then to the two locations you have pointed out and Stari Vitez, do you recall any other locations visited on 28th April 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we moved to the area which you call the bungalow, the Swiss cottage. At this point, the HVO commanders left the vehicles and entered the building.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Let me ask you about that incident, but why do you not have a seat to be more comfortable and if there are other locations on the map we can return to it when we have concluded this incident that I would like to ask you about. In the bungalow, there was a HVO soldier, I take it, who was both screaming and brandishing his pistol, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: He appeared visibly distraught?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: This went on for several minutes, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would say no more than five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: This went on in the presence of General Petkovic, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did he appear visibly distressed by this conduct in his presence? Did he scream at the soldier himself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he did not.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did he say anything to the soldier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he did not.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did anyone disarm this distraught HVO soldier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Eventually, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: After about five minutes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: By that stage, he had gone outside of the building. Prior to that, the commander, who General Petkovic was talking to, said something to the soldier, and then a number of other soldiers gestured to him. As I say, I could not understand the situation, although there was an interpreter there. It was not a situation where we could stand there and help each other interpret what was being said.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did you conclude anything from that incident about the HVO in general or HVO soldiers at the rank and file level?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that point, I got the impression that yes, initially there did not seem to be too much commander control.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Let us return to the issue of locations -- strike that. Did you conclude that because this threatening behaviour had gone on in the presence of the highest ranking military commander of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, although during the six months in Bosnia, that was the one and only isolated incident that I had ever come across.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Of that type, I take it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of any type.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Just a question of organising our time. Do you want to have a break now, do you have more questions, Mr Hayman?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I think if we take a break I can conclude in another ten questions or so, your Honour. I can perhaps be more efficient if we take a short break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Always efficient, but we will have a 20 minute break and we shall resume at 4.40.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The hearing is resumed. Please bring in the accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Let the witness in as well. We are going to resume, Mr Hayman.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Maybe I am causing the problem, the technical problem with my button, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Is everything all right, are you rested a little?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Fine, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Fine. Mr Hayman.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr President. Sergeant Major, returning to the issue of frontline visits on 28th April 1993, other than the locations you noted, did you also visit the frontline in the area of Kula to the northeast of Busovaca, with Generals Petkovic and Halilovic; do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I do not recall that at all.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Do you recall any visit to the northeast of Busovaca, in the Kula, Merdani, Dusana area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not that I recall.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Any other visits you recall on that day, other than the ones we have discussed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: In the course of these visits to frontline locations, did the two Generals meet with their troops and try and persuade them that the cease-fire should be obeyed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the course of the visits, apart from the bungalow, on all occasions both commanders left the vehicles and discussed amongst themselves and the soldiers on the ground; what their discussions, I do not know, as I was only there as escort.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Had you been -- sorry. Had you been told that was one of the purposes for these visits, to persuade the troops to obey and respect the cease-fire?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was briefed basically to escort both Generals around the positions that they wished to visit with the aim of those speaking to their soldiers on the ground and I presume to continue with a cease-fire and also to return to the positions that they occupied prior to the fighting that started to occur on the 16th.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Thank you. I had asked you whether you visited Stari Vitez on 16th April and I meant to ask about the 17th April, so if you could direct your attention to 17th April 1993, did you visit the headquarters of the Army of BiH in Stari Vitez on that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Do you recall visiting that headquarters any time during the 17th, 18th, 19th April 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: During that time, no.

utterances.speaker: MR HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did you visit an ABiH headquarters in Kruscica during that time period?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you, Sergeant Major, your Honour, that concludes my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr Hayman. I am now turning to Mr Kehoe. Mr Kehoe, you have the right to another examination. Do you want to add on anything, remaining within the scope of the cross-examination, of course?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr President, just very briefly, and directed to the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: Sergeant Major, you were asked some questions by Mr Hayman concerning the Hotel Vitez and you going into the Hotel Vitez with General Petkovic and seeing soldiers in black and camouflage; do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: When you went into the Hotel Vitez, was there a person behind a reception desk, a soldier, as you walked past?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, on the right-hand side was a reception desk where there was soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: Were civilians coming and going into the Hotel Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, there were no civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: Was your impression at the time that this was a military facility?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My impression was yes, that it was a military facility.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: You were asked some questions concerning -- if I might ask the assistance of the usher, and if we can flip down to 45, thank you. You stated in response to a question by Mr Hayman that the bell area was the area that you covered, but that you saw soldiers in approximately one quarter of that bell, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: Could you take the red marker and colour in the area where you saw those soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Witness marks map).

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: Staying there if you will, moving to another series of questions asked by Mr Hayman, he also asked you to identify the location of where the young boy was that was depicted in the photograph Exhibit 152/1 and 152/2; do you recall that, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: Could you take the green pen and give us the location of where that young boy was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Witness marks map).

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: You can have a seat, Sergeant Major. For the record, on the exhibit you have put another green marker on the lower right hand portion of the exhibit, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: That is Exhibit 45F. You were asked by Mr Hayman whether or not you saw where any artillery and mortars landed on 17th April when you were watching the spotter on the top of the hill, do you recall those questions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I recall the questions.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: You stated that you did not see where it landed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you hear it fire?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I heard two rounds being fired.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: Do you know if it was artillery or mortar fire?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was difficult at that stage, because all you got was a report of the weapon being fired, so it was difficult to assess whether it was mortar or artillery.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: But as a professional soldier, was it your opinion it was one or the other?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In my opinion, I would say more than likely it would be mortar.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr Hayman asked you a few questions about an incident involving an HVO soldier at the bungalow when you brought General Petkovic to the bungalow; do you recall those questions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I recall the questions.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: That particular soldier was out of control, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was to me very emotionally upset.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: Have you seen soldiers in the British army out of control in front of officers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I have seen that situation before.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: How was it handled in the British army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It will be handled in a manner that in a similar situation, the commander would leave it to his lower commanders to deal with that situation. He would not get involved himself.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: Is that not what happened in the bungalow, when the commander told someone to take care of this soldier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: By late April 1993, you had been in the theatre for approximately six months, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say that you had daily contact with the HVO soldiers at checkpoints et cetera?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: Did they operate with a chain of command and obey orders, based on your experience?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Beyond the scope, your Honour. If we are going to have new opinions based on new facts, we have to be able to cross-examine that new opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr President, this is in response to an issue that was brought up on cross-examination by Mr Hayman. That is all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: It was mentioned during the cross-examination, I believe, Mr Hayman. Please carry on, Mr Kehoe, but do not ask for new opinions. Try and remain very strictly within the scope of the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Sergeant Major, did the soldiers, HVO soldiers that you met follow orders and follow a chain of command, based on your experience?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, based on my experience on numerous occasions, mainly I would say at checkpoints, that they would not allow us to go through the checkpoints until they had conferred with higher command and on occasions they would go and get that authority for us to move through the checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Mr President, thank you. Thank you, Sergeant Major.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Sergeant Major, the judges are going to put questions to you. I am now turning to Judge Riad.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Sergeant Major Hughes, I would like to ask you some questions which happen not to be military questions, but questions to enlighten me on some of the points you raised. Perhaps you can use, let us say, language which I can understand. On 16th April, you moved in the old town of Vitez, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: You noticed an attack on the old part of Vitez, an attack on the Muslim area; I am just speaking in general terms. There was an attack on the Muslim area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: Was there any fighting there or was it one-sided attack? Were there two armies fighting, or was it a one-sided attack?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In my opinion, it was a one-sided attack.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: A one-sided attack. I will ask almost a similar question concerning Putis and Jelinak. When you went into Jelinak, you made a cursory search, as you said. You found first some houses burnt down, food on table and bullet holes on the door handles. Was there any sign also of fighting there, or did it also look too as a one-sided attack on civilians?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It looked as though it was a one-sided attack on civilians. Also in that situation, around the villages, every animal had also been killed and in my opinion, an attack had taken place and the civilian occupants of that particular village had fled in a hurry.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes. It looked like being taken by surprise, because you found food on the tables and people as if they were leading their normal life, their daily life.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that was the opinion I got by going through the houses, is the houses were just left.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: It was not to suppress a revolt or an uprising, or that sort of thing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not in my opinion, no.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: You went on and mentioned to us something about the 94 corpses which you showed us being buried. Was there any forensic investigation showing how they died? Were they executed or were they shot in a random way or were they fighting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From what I could see, there was no forensic being carried out while we were there. These bodies, I am under the impression, had been in the gymnasium of the school for some days, but clearly because you could see through the plastic bags, of the bodies that were brought out, I only saw one through the plastic bag that was wearing camouflage clothing. The remainder were all wearing civilian clothing.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: You saw two decapitated, I think.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: And teenagers and women?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not recognise at that stage whether they were male or female, but they were two bodies with two small bags either side of the bodies, which at first I thought were small children, i.e. babies, because of the size of the package. On closer examination, it was the heads to the bodies that they were lying beside.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: So it was not shooting, it was decapitating.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Whether the bodies had any gunshot wounds I could not say.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: No investigation was done?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: On 16th April, you saw on your way coming back from Breza you observed glow in the dark from Putis and Jelinak. Was this almost simultaneous to what was happening in Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not that I am aware of.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: Which day was that? You said it was 16th April.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would say prior to the 16th, so it could possibly be the 14th or 15th. The 16th April we moved into Vitez because of the fighting.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: It was the day before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was possibly the day before or the day before that, on the way back.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: To your knowledge, was there any army there, BiH Army attacking, or that sort of thing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, as we drove past again, due to the terrain, we could only see the glow of the burning. Again, we continued to move, we did not stop and I did not hear any gunfire.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: You mentioned also a column of, you said Muslims, moving around and a number of refugees frightened, I think that was -- I think it was on the 17th, they looked frightened and so on. Where were they coming from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The line of refugees were on the main Vitez to Zenica bypass. They were coming from the east, so they were coming from maybe the Ahmici area or that area, moving towards the Dubravica road junction.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: Were they attacked on the way or did they pass --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they were just moving. They were not in a group, they were quite strung out along the road, moving in that direction.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: You mentioned this lady, this lady crawling on the pavement, and you apparently had to protect her until she reached a safe area. Was there any shooting, any snipers? How would be an old woman killed in the street?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would presume that -- at that stage I did not know whether she was wounded or not, she was crawling along the wall of a house on the pavement of the street. At that time, again, I cannot say that I heard any gunfire, I just positioned the vehicle what I thought that would give her some form of protection, wherever the fire may be coming from, so she could get into some form of cover.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: You do not know where the shooting was coming from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not at that stage, no.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: Were there other people in the same condition?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was nobody else in that same condition, but where the woman crawled to, they were another three or four people, all civilians, that were quite concerned of the situation. When I returned there, I went obviously round a loop and returned back via that position, and it was at that stage that they were indicating to me that she had been shot and were asking for assistance. Again, though I did not hear any gunfire, I felt that the situation did not warrant me allowing soldiers out of the back of the vehicle to at that stage treat the woman for gunshot wounds.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: Coming back to Jelinak, you said that it was a mixed village with Croats and Muslims.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR KEHOE
utterances.text: You said some of the houses were burnt. Were they Muslim houses? Could you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
